title: SOFA: A Compute-Memory Optimized Sparsity Accelerator via Cross-Stage Coordinated Tiling
problem: Existing dynamic sparse accelerators for large-scale token parallel processing (LTPP) in Transformer inference focus on single-stage optimization and computational improvements, missing cross-stage memory optimization opportunities and causing excessive memory access and redundant computation.
motivation: As large language models become increasingly prevalent, efficient high-throughput inference acceleration is critical to enable practical deployment at scale.
method: SOFA uses three coordinated techniques to optimize sparse neural network processing: (1) predicting where attention will be sparse using simple log-based math (adding only, no subtraction) to detect patterns with minimal overhead, (2) sorting data within stages and passing sorted results forward to enable fine-grained coordination between stages using FlashAttention, and (3) a dedicated SOFA hardware accelerator that exploits this cross-stage coordination to reduce redundant memory fetches and processing time. The key is coordinating decisions across pipeline stages instead of optimizing each stage independently, which avoids redundant computation and excessive memory access.
key_novelty: The core innovation is enabling lightweight, fine-grained coordination of data flow across pipeline stages in dynamic sparse computation to avoid the excessive memory access that occurs when each stage optimizes independently.
contributions: Leading zero computing paradigm for efficient attention sparsity prediction via log-based operations
Distributed sorting and sorted updating FlashAttention mechanism with cross-stage coordinated tiling
SOFA accelerator hardware design for Transformer sparse inference
Comprehensive evaluation demonstrating 9.5x speedup and 71.5x energy efficiency vs A100, and 9.3-15.8x improvements vs eight SOTA accelerators
